FRIDAY, APRIL 30, 1926: A. M.
The meeting was called to order at 9:45 A. M. by Brother Babst.
The roll was called and the minutes of the previous meeting read
and approved.
Committee reports were then called for by the President of the
Convention. The Committee on Credentials reported that no dele
gates had yet presented credentials from the Nu or Beta chapters.
The Committee on New Business reported that wires had been sent
as directed by the Convention in the previous meeting and recom
mended a meeting of a committee of the whole at 2 o'clock to hear the
petitions of organizations desiring admission to Psi Upsilon.
It was moved, seconded and passed to accept this report and refer
it .to the Committee on Annual Communications.
The Committee to Nominate for the Executive Council announced
its decision to renominate Brother Walter T. Collins to his present
office and for the second vacancy Brother Archibald Douglas, Lamb
da '94.
It was moved, seconded and passed to accept this report. It was
moved, seconded and passed to elect the nominees on a single ballot.
The Committee on Annual Communications reported the follow
ing resolutions :
I. Resolved, that the annual communication from the Executive Coun
cil be accepted as submitted.
2. Resolved, that the Treasurer's report be accepted as submitted.
3. Resolved, that inasmuch as it was Brother Bridgman's personal re
quest that a Centennial Fund be established by the Chapters, each delegate at
each convention shall be asked to report the progress of his chapter in collect
ing the annual tax of $2 per undergraduate member.
4. Resolved, that Psi Upsilon resign from the Interfraternity Conference.
5. Resolved, that each Chapter select an alumnus as its representative
with whom the Executive Council might have contact the same as with the
active chapter.
6. Resolved, that this Convention recommend that each Chapter appoint
an alumnus or undergraduate as Chapter historian.
It was moved, seconded and passed that the report be accepted.
The several resolutions were then duly adopted by the Convention.
The Committee on Unfinished Business announced that it would
present no report.

Brother Babst carried to the Convention the greetings and good
wishes of Brother Houston of the Executive Council and his regrets
at not being able to be present at the Convention.
Brother Corcoran reported on The Diamond Life Membership
Drive and called attention to the need of earnest effort in the cam
paign if the continued publication of The Diamond is to be assured.
Brother Babst then called upon the delegates of various chapters for
opinions and suggestions relative to The Diamond. Every delegate
who spoke believed The Diamond a vital factor in the fraternity and
assured the Convention of the intention of his Chapter to push the
Life Membership drive to success. The suggestion was made that
extra copies be mailed out by the Chapters to their alumni.
Brother Babst summarized the suggestions and points made in
the course of the discussion, and it was moved, seconded and passed
to extend the time limit for the Drive to January i, 1927.
After a brief announcement of the work confronting the after
noon session, the President of the Convention called upon the Chi to
continue the oral reports of Chapters by roll call. Reports were com
pleted as far as the Epsilon.
Brother Babst then directed a few remarks to the subject of im
proving scholarship as mentioned in the reports of the delegates and
discussed by the Executive Council. He urged a serious considera
tion of the present situation with a view to preventing further undesir
able developments.
It was moved, seconded and passed to adjourn and reconvene at
two o'clock.
Meeting adjourned 11 :45 A. M.
FRIDAY AFTERNOON, APRIL 30, 1926
Convention called to order at 2:05 P. M. by Brother Backus,
first Vice President of the Convention. The minutes of the previous
meeting were read and approved.
The Committee on Credentials reported that delegates from
the Nu and Beta Chapters had arrived and been accredited :
Beta�R. S. Wheelock, '26.

It was moved, seconded and passed to resolve the Convention into
a Committee of the Whole to hear an address of welcome by Dean

John R. Effinger of the University of Michigan. Brother Collins
took the chair and Brother Backus introduced the speaker.
Following a brief talk by Dean Effinger, the Convention again
resumed formal session, and Brother Naylor addressed a few remarks
to the subject of scholarship in the chapters.
The motion was made, seconded and passed that the petitions of
Pi Upsilon, The Wranglers and Epsilon Phi be taken from the table.
The Committee on New Business then reported the following
resolutions :
I. Resolved, that this Convention suggest to the Beta, Gamma, Delta,
Sigma, Beta Beta, Delta Delta, Lambda, Psi, Pi and Tau chapters that
they endeavor to send junior delegates to the initiations of adjacent chapters,
thereby fostering a closer and more frequent fraternal contact.
2. Resolved, that this Convention earnestly urges that all the Chapters of
Psi Upsilon raise their scholastic requirements for initiation in a marked
degree above those of the University in which they are located, thereby reliev
ing the present acute loss of men in freshman and sophomore delegations due
mainly to scholarship.
3. Resolved, that the individual chapters of this Fraternity realize more
fully their obligations to the college of which they are only a part, and appre
ciate the fact that no part is as great as the whole; that Psi Upsilon depends
on American colleges and universities for its existence, and that everjmember of this fraternity should look upon Psi Upsilon first, only after his
Alma Mater.
4. Resolved, that the undergraduate associate editors of The Diamond
spend more thoughtful time in the preparations for communications in order to
reach their own alumni through collegiate appeal as well as fraternal and
chapter appeal ; that extra copies of The Diamond be sent by the undergraduate
editors to their alumni non-subscribers in an effort to aid the present subscrip
tion drive.
S- Resolved, that The Diamond Committee be instructed to bind the six
volumes of The Diamond and send such copies to the chapters for use in their
libraries ; cost expense of such binding to be borne by the chapters.
The five resolutions presented by the Committee were adopted
as submitted.
It was moved, seconded and passed that a vote of thanks be
tendered the Phi Chapter as hosts to the Convention.
The motion was made, seconded and passed to resolve the Con
vention into a Committee of the Whole to hear the petitioning or
ganizations. Brother Collins was then appointed Chairman of the
Committee of the Whole by Brother Backus.

APPENDIX A
Annual Communication of the Executive Council to the 1926
Convention of Psi Upsilon
At this convention held in the ninety-third year of our fraternity,
the Executive Council extends its felicitations to all the Chapters
through their delegates and congratulates the fraternity and all of its
twenty-six chapters upon the continued preservation of the high ideals
of our brotherhood. We look forward to the future with renewed
confidence and assurance that the diamond of Psi Upsilon shall never
sparkle less.
It is well at this time to recall that in establishing our fraternity
our founders had in mind the creation of a spiritual body. This or
ganization is not one conducted for business or professional purposes
but is one organized to develop year by year, in the various delega
tions as they pass down the ages, that spirit of brotherhood based on
our ideals and our genuine, friendly contacts. Some fraternities have
gone in for various services to their members and have become large
organized bodies but Psi Upsilon has always kept to the simplicity
of its original purpose, realizing that the strength of the fraternity
lies with the undergraduates whose voice is expressed through the
annual convention. We have yet to see that the confidence placed in
the undergraduates has in any way been violated and we feel that it
is a remarkable proof of the soundness of our principle that through
all these years the purpose and personnel of Psi Upsilon has remained
on the same high level.
This was the conception of our fraternity of the late and our
beloved President, Herbert L. Bridgman. In these days of over-or
ganized and material purpose of any kind of cooperative effort he
always kept clearly before us that high star of our function, namely,
that we are a body primarily and almost entirely for the purpose of
developing the spiritual side of our lives, which side we sometimes
feel nowadays is in so many ways neglected. That is why our alumni
so often turn back in their thoughts to Psi Upsilon and why Psi Upsi
lon holds a place so near to the heart of all of us.

�
II �
ALUMNI MEETING
This devotion to our fraternity was splendidly evidenced in New
York on March the 13th when forty alumni representatives from our
various Psi Upsilon clubs and associations and other alumni bodies
gathered together to discuss informally the affairs of our
fraternity.
The purpose of this meeting was clearly set forth by Brother Babst
in the invitation which in part read :
"One of the sources of the strength of Psi Upsilon has been the simplicity
of its organization. The Chapters are supreme. Large powers have been dele
gated to the Executive Council, but in practice the Council defers to the Annual
Convention. So successful has been this course that it is now highly praised by
those fraternities who have embarked on extensive systems of organization.
At the outset, therefore, it is desired that the suggestions above be regarded in
no wise as a step away from our traditional policies but rather an aid to
sustain them."
One of the principal suggestions that came out of our Alumni
Meeting was that each chapter select an Alumnus as its representa
tive with whom the Council might have contact the same as with the
active chapter. If at the present time any chapter has a board of
Trustees the President of this Board or one of the Trustees might
well be designated as this Alumni representative or if there is any
other alumni organization intimately associated with the chapter a
representative might be selected from that organization. The Secre
tary of the Council then would send to this alumni representative all
communications that he sends to the chapters looking to him to help
in keeping the Alumni of the chapter in closer touch with the under
graduates. There are many ways that such an alumni representative
of the chapters would be most helpful and the Council trusts that this
convention will follow the suggestion of our Alumni Meeting in pass
ing a resolution toward this end.
NECROLOGY
While a number of our brothers have passed to the great beyond
since the last convention, we have in the last few years not listed
them in our annual communications since a complete record of them
is kept by the Diamond but we at this time would ask the convention
to rise for a moment in silent tribute to those brothers who are no
longer with us.

12 �
MASTER OF THE ROLLS
Following the recommendation of the last convention in resolu
tion No. 6, during the past year. Brother A. Avery Hallock of the
Council, who was
appointed National Master of the Rolls has been
engaged in correcting and systematizing the address lists of the chap
ters. All of the chapters have prepared address lists of their mem
bers and sent them to the Council ; but many of these lists have been
incomplete and inaccurate and some of them have only recently reach
ed Brother Llallock. It is of the utmost importance that the chap
ters keep their address lists up to date. To this end previous conven
tions have ordered that each chapter appoint an Alumnus Master of
the Rolls and two undergraduate Masters of the Rolls to assist him.
If any Alumnus Master of the Rolls fails to do the work for which
he was appointed, his chapter should, without hesitation, appoint an
other in his place. For this reason it is obvious that no alumnus
should be appointed to this important position without his consent and
approval. The undergraduate Masters of the Rolls should be ap
pointed each spring for the ensuing year and should, preferably, be a
Freshman and a Sophomore (who will be, respectively. Sophomore
and Junior during their active term). The Sophomore should be re
appointed the following spring, if possible, to ensure continuity of
experience. Their names should be reported to the Secretary of the
Council immediately on their appointment and they will receive ex
plicit instructions as to their duties from the National Master of the
Rolls.
CATALOGUE
The Council has decided that it would be better to postpone the
issue of any supplement to the general catalogue until about the time
of our Centennial, when a new and complete catalogue should be
issued. Therefore, it is very evident why the addresses of all the
Alumni should be correct.
HISTORIAN
In compliance with resolution No. i of our last convention, each
chapter has been asked to appoint an historian. The Council would
suggest that an Alumnus be selected who would write a general his
tory of the chapter from the issuance of the last Epitome, so that, at

�
13 �
the time of our centennial a new Epitome may be issued and contain
a rather complete history of each chapter of the fraternity. By this
history is not meant a detailed statement, delegation by delegation,
but a general story as to how the chapter has developed in relation
to its college or university, what it did during the war, and other
general matters.
This would preserve at the Chapters an accurate chapter history
and at the same time provide material for the future historians of our
Fraternity. There is usually some brother in each chapter well qual
ified and interested in this fascinating work. To set our archives and
historical material in better order would be a real contribution to the
fraternity.
SCHOLARSHIP
In response to resolution No. 5 at the last convention the Council
has been urging a higher standard of scholarship. This may sound
like an old and hackneyed subject but the Council is very serious in
emphasizing the importance of this matter. Some of our chapters
have been woefully lax in this regard. On this subject Professor
George H. Nettleton of the Beta, and a member of the Council, gave
a splendid address at our Alumni Meeting, which address we hope to
have shortly in the hands of every Psi Upsilon undergraduate as well
as of a great many Psi Upsilon Alumni.
DIAMOND
The Council wishes to state that the Diamond is proving more and
more of a success and the Council considers it an excellent medium to
weld together and maintain the spirit of our fraternity. A great deal
of credit and praise is due the men who have had direct charge of
the Diamond especially Brother Corcoran. Theirs has been surely
a labor of love for the fraternity. It has been a hard task to get out
each issue but the work is being gradually made lighter. Any effort,
however, is made more pleasant by the hearty support of the recipi
ents and we are glad to see that the campaign for life members has
been partially successful and we feel that it will be fully successful
now that it has been extended to Founder's Day, next November.
There is not an undergraduate or an Alumnus who has given serious

attention to the Diamond and realizes its value and the work involved,
who is not in favor of it and glad to support it, not only with their ten
dollar life subscription, but in every other way.
It has been suggested that sufficient copies of each issue of the
Diamond should be retained so that a later time these copies might be
bound and sent to the chapters to serve as a current history of the
fraternity. It might be well for the convention to authorize the
Council to have the six copies bound for the chapters and then when
each chapter receives its copies the chapter could reimburse the Coun
cil at cost.
CENTENNIAL FUND
The Council would call particular attention of the chapters to
resolution No. 4 of last year requiring each chapter to set aside each
year $2.00 for each undergraduate toward a Centennial Fund. The
Council would recommend that at each convention between now and
the Centennial a roll call of the chapters be made and a report given
as to the condition of the Centennial Fund of each. This is a matter
which is very easy to keep up if the assessments are made each year
but if any chapter is lax they will soon find themselves in a serious
difficulty in maintaining their proportionate share of the fund.

-15The Council regrets that the other chapters have not been visited
but they will be either at the end of this collegiate year or the early
part of next year. It must be remembered that the members of the
Council visit the chapters on their own time and since such visits are
entirely -voluntary, a member of the Council quite often has to visit
the chapter when it is most convenient for him to do so. Members of
the Council look upon these visits as a conscientious duty and en
deavor to the best of their ability to perform them.
ELECTION TO THE COUNCIL
The Council would call to the attention of the convention at this
time that the terms of Brothers Walter T. Collins and George H.
Nettleton, as members of the Executive Council expire. It is neces
sary for the convention to elect two brothers to the Council for the
usual term of five years.
INITIATIONS
In view of resolution No. 7 of the last convention the Council has
urged and does urge the members to increase the ceremonial part of
their initiation. We are glad to see that satisfactory progress has
been made in this regard. All initiations should be conducted with
more dignity and less horse play since Psi Upsilon is a society of
men and not preparatory school boys. So much beauty can be brought
into the initiation ceremony and such a lasting impression can be
piven to brothers entering our bonds that everything possible should
be done to make the ceremony and everything relative to it an
inspir
ing and dignified procedure.
PETITIONS
The Council has received petitions from the following societies
and refers them to the convention :
Epsilon Phi of McGill University
The Wranglers of Northwestern University
Pi Upsilon of the University of Kansas.
Representatives from these petitioning bodies are present and the
Council would ask that they be given a respectful hearing.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE COUNCIL
AND FINANCES OF CHAPTERS
The Council would not only ask but must insist that the chapters
answer all communications from the Council or its officers promptly
and that each chapter keep the finances of its chapter up to date and
in commendable condition.
INTERFRATERNITY CONFERENCE
The Council would recommend to the fraternity that Psi Upsilon
resign from the Interfraternity Conference as small benefit comes
from this affiliation and it is a needless expense and contact.
LESS RESOLUTIONS
The Council would heartily recommend to the Convention and
particularly to the resolution committee that less resolutions be passed
at the conventions for a few years. The chapters already are loaded
with requirements which the conventions have passed by resolutions
and have at the present time about all they can do to keep up with
these requirements. While Psi Upsilon wants to be active and to ac
complish everything that is necessary, yet the Council does not feel
that it is desirable to pass resolutions merely for the sake of passing
them and with the result of requiring the chapters to do any more at
present, at least, than is now expected.
CONDUCT AT CONVENTION
It is almost unnecessary to urge the delegates at this convention
to comply with resolution No. 6 of the last convention, which reads
as follows :
"The delegates to this convention have been selected by their respective
chapters in conformance with the desires of the Fraternity as duly expressed in
a resolution at the 1924 convention. The Council wrote each chapter on April
i6th last, quoting this resolution concerning the use of intoxicating liquors at or
during convention and your presence here is evidence that you are in full sym
pathy with the Convention Resolution, regardless of your, personal opinions.
"Let us have no misunderstandings, and from the outset of the convention
let us all resolve to obey this injunction which applies to delegates and guests,
undergraduates, alike. The reputation of the Fraternity and more particularly
of our hosts�
the Pi Chapter�
must be zealously guarded The will of the

The convention at the Pi Chapter last year was in every way so
successful and the conduct of the delegates so commendable that we
feel surely that at this convention at the Phi Chapter the same stand
ard will be set and the record maintained.
With every good wish to each and every delegate, to all the Alum
ni present and to all brothers of our fraternity.
Respectfully and fraternally submitted.
Executive Counch,

APPENDIX B
Report of the Treasurer
I. In the attached balance sheet the decrease for the year in the
General Fund is largely due to special appropriations for the expense
of publishing The Diamond during the period of building up the
Diamond Endowment Fund to a point where the income from In
vestments will carry such expense. Substantial progress has been
made in this direction, the Fund having been increased by life sub
scriptions from $8,978.81 shown in last year's report to $17,913.79
as of April 6, 1926 (practically doubled).
Receipts are invested as received and bond investments now ag
gregate $18,000 par value with an annual coupon interest return of
$815.00.
2. In the General Fund investment account $1,000 par value
Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul Convertible 4>^% bond was sold at
51% because of the Receivership of this railroad, showing a loss of
$493.82 indicated in Schedule "A" under Expenditures, but this was
more than offset by the sale of $1,000 par value Chesapeake & Ohio
Convertible 5% bond at 148 (cost 95) representing a profit of $531.78
also shown in Schedule "A" under Income.
3. At the date of compilation of this report all Chapters have
paid annual Chapter taxes, except Pi Chapter which is in arrears to
General Fund tax of $87.75.
Respectfully and fraternally submitted,
Walter T. Collins, Treasurer.
April 6th, 1926.
